page.text:
An argument is not merely a sequence of true sentences. It is a claim
that a conclusion is forced by stated premises. Logic formalizes this
claim in two complementary ways: semantically, by truth in every model;
syntactically, by derivation according to explicit inference rules. A
mature proof moves fluently between these viewpoints while never hiding
which assumptions are active.
